During a fierce storm, the ship sank, taking the amulet to the bottom of the lake. Over time, a colossal monster appeared in these waters, covered in armor-like scales that made it nearly invincible. The Armored Bighead has been spotted during its hunting raids, sinking ships and boats that cross its territory. It is believed that the creature swallowed the magical amulet, which caused its transformation, granting it incredible strength and impenetrable protection.

fish.name: Barbel-Ghost
fish.description: This ghostly creature is not a regular Barbel. It is much larger, and its translucent body emanates dim, deadly light. There is no doubt that spirits from the other world are controlling it.

fish.name: Black Vampire Gar
fish.description: Black Vampire Gar is one creepy blood-sucking Monster that can be caught in the Mudwater River only at night on Halloween. This Dracula-fish may not be too big, weighing around 7-10 kg (15-22 lb), but it sure is one scary critter! So make sure to have the right tackle - this experience will be unforgettable!

fish.name: Bluegill Skeleton
fish.description: Oops…looks like this poor Bluegill was devoured by a real predator!

fish.name: Buzzman Tambaqui
fish.description: Everyone's a little bit Irish on St. Patrick’s Day! Even in South America. Having sipped some festive beer, this Tambaqui decided to go on a bit of a bender and start an Irish-themed party across all tropical reservoirs. Even though this Tambaqui looks like a Piranha, he is a kind merry-maker at heart. Lure him with the Pickled Jauari Palm Fruit and catch him for a prize. They say that if you catch a lot of these fish, you can get a bright celebratory Irish Beanie Hat!

fish.name: Carp-Ghost
fish.description: The spirits that have possessed this large Carp are definitely not friendly. On Halloween, guided by the full moon, a host of abominations has broken into our world through the otherworldly gates, and this creature was among them.

fish.name: Catfish-Demon
fish.description: On Halloween, the gates between our world and the beyond allow hideous demons to cross. They have powerful Catfish bodies with an unusual dark blue tint, blue irises with vertical pupils and four horns — aren't they the most frightening creatures?

fish.name: Crystal Burbot
fish.description: Crystal Burbot (Lota Crystallo) is a mystical fish that can be caught only at Christmas time. According to an old angling legend, this once voracious cold-blooded predator was turned to crystalline form by the Ice Queen for eating her magic white mice. And while this version might sound like childish nonsense, no one has yet come up with a better explanation for the existence of a crystal-bodied fish. Go figure.

fish.name: Dingonek
fish.description: The Dingonek is a massive creature, weighing up to 155 kg (340 lbs), with a head resembling a lioness marked like a leopard, and two long white fangs protruding from its upper jaw. Its broad back, covered in armadillo-like scales, is reminiscent of a hippo's. A wide, finned tail allows it to stay afloat in swift currents. Some believe it may be a descendant of prehistoric reptiles that survived in remote regions, though no bones or skin samples have been found. Eyewitness accounts, however, leave little room for doubt about its existence.

fish.name: Double Head Eel
fish.description: The Double Head Eel (Anguilla Bicephalus) is a terror of the depths that frightens even the most experienced anglers. This mutated predator, weighing up to 35 kg (77 lbs), has two fully functional heads, each with its own mind and an insatiable hunger for hunting. Its snake-like body is covered in slime that releases toxins, paralyzing its prey upon contact. The Double Head Eel can attack from both sides simultaneously, making it nearly unbeatable in close combat. It breaks through underwater obstacles and attacks from unexpected angles. It is said that its appearance is always accompanied by electrical storms, as if nature itself is warning of the danger.

fish.name: Fierce Muskie
fish.description: Hiding in underwater thickets and under snags, this burning Monster tirelessly seeks out new defenseless victims. The spirit of fire endowed it with unbridled malice and unquenchable bloodthirstiness.

fish.name: Fire Muskie
fish.description: The otherworldly spirits endowed this disgusting creature with exorbitant gluttony. This Muskie devastates reservoirs, gobbling up all the fish clean. Its glowing, fiery body glides through underwater vegetation, leaving no chance for survival for anyone.

fish.name: Frankenfish
fish.description: Frankenfish (Monstrum Ichtiandras) - a bizarre result of an originally innocent prank gone wrong, this infernal abomination was sewn together from different fish parts by a fisherman’s son to give his angling friends a good fright on Halloween. On that dark and stormy night, just as the boy prepared to pull the monstrosity out of the water and terrify his pals, a bolt of lightning struck the water and the gruesome creature miraculously came to life! With a powerful jerk the monster pulled our unexpecting prankster into the dark water abyss...

fish.name: Furry Trout
fish.description: Furry Trout (Oncorhynchus Furrycus) this legendary fish belongs to the Trout family and is believed to be a nonexistent hoax by most anglers. Legend has it, that the Furry Trout is more ferocious than the Himalayan Yeti, more ruthless than the Loch Ness Monster! And yet...the white furry floof is actually cute as hell! Similar in size and appearance to its direct relative, the Rainbow Trout, Furry Trout is the result of evolutionary metamorphosis. The poor thing had to grow thick fluffy fur in order to keep itself warm and survive in the severe cold waters of its harsh northern environment. Aww...

fish.name: Ghost Pike
fish.description: Ghost Pike (Esox Spiritus). Wow! Looks like you’re terribly in luck! You managed to catch the mysterious Ghost Pike - a rare anomaly that’s been spotted in many of America’s waterways this Halloween. Some find it terrifyingly mystical, others tend to believe there’s simple radiation involved. Whatever the case may be, this monster Pike is glowing like a real ghost and now you can tell everyone about catching one!

fish.name: Grass Carp-Ghost
fish.description: Evil spirits have possessed a large specimen of the Grass Carp. Now this creature is devouring all aquatic vegetation of the reservoir, threatening its ecological balance.

fish.name: Green Ogre Gar
fish.description: Green Ogre Gar is a true Monster menace that roams the quiet waters of Neherrin at night around Halloween. Weighing around 11-15 kg (24-34 lb), this is one tough mutant to catch. But oh boy, are you in for some excitement while trying.

fish.name: Hellish Muskie
fish.description: A huge fish glowing with a fiery haze has appeared in the reservoir, eating everyone smaller than itself. This abomination entered our world on Halloween, when the fabric of reality between the worlds became very thin. And it looks like this creature is not in a hurry to leave.

fish.name: Hybrid Carp-Ghost
fish.description: At first glance, this fish looks like a particularly large Hybrid Carp, but the ghostly light emanating from its translucent body indicates otherwise.

fish.name: Largemouth Bass-Phantom
fish.description: On Halloween, these predatory fish turned into glowing monsters and took over the whole reservoir, terrorizing its inhabitants. It is said that flickering lights can be spotted over the water surface where they live.

fish.name: Leather Carp-Ghost
fish.description: You would never have seen this possessed Carp if not for the otherworldly gates that opened on Halloween. Now this creature has intimidated the inhabitants of the reservoir so much that they are scared to move and find some food.

fish.name: Leprechaun Fish
fish.description: Leprechaun Fish (Leprechaunus Ichtiandrus) - a small fish, shamrock green in color that is by some believed to be a myth. But every year on St. Patrick’s Day there are reports of a very fishy anomaly. Legend has it, that long ago one very hungry Green Sunfish found the leprechaun’s pot of gold at the end of the rainbow and...ate it! So if you engage in a fierce fish fight with what seems to be a monster the size of a Trophy Catfish...don’t be too stunned to land an adversary no bigger than your typical sunfish! True or not, believe it or not, but you should definitely try your luck at catching the Leprechaun Fish.

fish.name: Mirror Carp-Ghost
fish.description: This massive Mirror Carp has become a receptacle for evil spirits that have broken into our world through otherworldly gates. Now this translucent ghostly voracious creature is depriving the inhabitants of the reservoir of their food.

fish.name: Northern Snakehead
fish.description: Northern Snakehead ( Channa argus ) is a slick and agile thing, that looks like a real snake! The homeland of Snakehead is the rivers of the Far Eastern region. However today this sly one made its way into many reservoirs of Europe and America. And this is completely not good at all, because Snakehead belongs to the invasive species of predators. It grows quickly, quickly breeds, and quickly devours everything it can devour, including other fish, tadpoles, frogs, and even birds! Just imagine, this thing can live up to 5 days without water, burrowing in the silt, and is able to move on land in search of a new plentiful pond. With such appetites, it is not surprising that it can grow more than a meter in length and gain about 10 kg (22 lb) of weight. Usually it hides under snags and in waterplants in shallow water, preferring heavily overgrown areas. Help us all St. Patrick! If you don't stop this villain, the entire fauna of the reservoir will suffer!

fish.name: Prussian Carp-Ghost
fish.description: The pale light emitted by these creatures can hardly dispel the darkness of the depths of the other world that has disgorged these creatures. They glide in the water silently, scaring away the inhabitants of the reservoirs with their unnatural ghostly light.

fish.name: Rowdy Bass
fish.description: Rowdy Bass (Micropterus Debaucherous) Yeehaw! This is one tough barbaric beast to ride! The Rowdy Bass is such a rare occurrence in these waters, that only few are actually said to have seen them around St.Patrick’s Day. Hard to find and even harder to catch, given you’re lucky enough to land one on your hook, these debaucherous monsters will give you the fish fight of your life! And no wonder, the feisty character is in this fiery fish’s blood.

fish.name: Slide Rock Bolter
fish.description: The Slide-Rock Bolter (Macrostoma saxiperrumptus) is a bizarre and fearsome creature recounted by the lumberjacks of North America during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is believed to live in the mountains of Colorado. The creature has an immense head, small eyes, and a large mouth, weighing up to 160 kg (350 lbs). Its tail ends in a fluke similar to a dolphin, equipped with enormous grab-hooks. This fearsome animal uses the grab-hooks on its split tail to latch onto the crest of a mountain or ridge. Once it spots its prey, it lifts its tail to release its hold, then slides down, scooping its victims into its mouth. When not hunting, the Bolter resides in the depths of mountain lakes.

fish.name: Smallmouth Bass-Phantom
fish.description: The breath of the other world has changed the once ordinary predators. Now these glowing creatures have taken over the reservoir and are pestering its inhabitants. It is said that flickering lights can be spotted over the water surface where they live.

fish.name: Steelhead-Phantom
fish.description: An otherworldly glow emanates from within these creatures and instills mystical fear in everyone around. There are legends that Jack himself — yes, THAT Jack — was very fond of snacking on Salmons like this one.

fish.name: Sturgeon-Demon
fish.description: A demon has entered the otherworldly gates and possessed this Sturgeon, distorting it beyond recognition! Red-brown scales, vertical pupils, and forward-pointing horns — a truly chilling sight!

fish.name: Tarpon-Demon
fish.description: This otherworldly abomination hardly resembles a Tarpon anymore. Its blood-red color, infernal vertical pupils, and curved horns label it as a demon that has crossed into our world through the thinned fabric of reality.

fish.name: Trout-Ghost
fish.description: Exuding ghostly light, these creatures from the other world intimidate the whole reservoir. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

fish.name: Trout-Phantom
fish.description: This beautiful rainbow trout has been transformed into a terrible creature, glowing with otherworldly light and indiscriminately devouring all underwater dwellers. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

fish.name: Trout-Skeleton
fish.description: Only the otherworldly forces could bring such monsters to life! These skeletons once belonged to common Trouts, but they have now come to life to instill fear in the underwater dwellers. Vicious and bloodthirsty, they are the basis for the Golem.

fish.name: Vampire Biara
fish.description: Vampire Biara (Rhaphiodon vulpinus vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish, weighing up to 60 kg (132 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Biara feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

fish.name: Vampire Payara
fish.description: Vampire Payara (Hydrolycus Scomberoides vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish that can weigh up to 90 kg (198 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Payara feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

fish.name: Vampire Trahira
fish.description: Vampire Trahira (Hoplias Aimara vampyrus) is a terrifying predatory fish that can weigh up to 120 kg (264 lbs), with all teeth transformed into long, vampire-like fangs. Its venomous red scales and glowing eyes enhance its sinister appearance. Vampire Trahira feeds on the blood of its prey, sinking its sharp fangs into them. It inhabits shady backwaters and abandoned ships on the Amazon, stealthily patrolling the waters during foggy nights. These fish not only inspire fear with their appearance but also strike with sudden, deadly force.

fish.name: White Carp-Ghost
fish.description: In the pale, ghostly silhouette of this creature, one can hardly recognize the outlines of a huge Carp. It glides in the waters silently and unhurriedly, scaring away the unfortunate inhabitants of the reservoir with its existence alone.

fish.name: Historic Black Crappie
fish.description: Historic Black Crappie (Pomoxis Nigromaculatus) is a really fishy piece of history! This particular specimen bears a special anchor tag on its fin is marked with the year 1796 and engraved with President’s George Washington’s signature! Apparently, that very year a number of fish hatchlings were released on July 4th to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Indeed, a truly historic specimen!

fish.name: Historic Brown Trout
fish.description: Historic Brown Trout (Salmo Trutta) - this extremely rare specimen of Brown Trout is almost older than history itself! One of the special hatchlings that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence, the fish boasts an old anchor tag on its fin, marked with the year 1796 and President’s George Washington’s signature! Such cases of long-lifers among these historic fish are rare, but not entirely unknown to scientists, who have been trying in vain to solve this mystery for many years...

fish.name: Historic Bull Trout
fish.description: Historic Bull Trout (Salvelinus Confluentus) - this extremely rare specimen of Bull Trout is almost older than history itself! One of the special hatchlings that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence, the fish boasts an old anchor tag on its fin, marked with the year 1796 and President’s George Washington’s signature! Such cases of long-lifers among these historic fish are rare, but not entirely unknown to scientists, who have been trying in vain to solve this mystery for many years...

fish.name: Historic Butterfly Peacock Bass
fish.description: Peacock Bass (Cichla Ocellaris) is a popular and colorful game fish, that can be quite the fighter and is a very anticipated catch for any angler. But check this one out… Wow, looks like you didn’t just land a Trophy. This specimen is closer to being a miracle! Imagine, this very Peacock Bass you’re holding somehow managed to live for over 200 years and is a truly historic fish. As you can see from the anchor tag, this Peacock was released into these waters on 4th July 1796, to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence along with many other young fish! No doubt about it - the tag bears the release date and President George Washington's signature!

fish.name: Historic Chain Pickerel
fish.description: Chain Pickerel (Esox Niger) are known to have a very long lifespan. Throughout Europe there have been many cases of capturing Chain Pickerel over 100 years old! But it looks like this American specimen has outlived them all - just imagine, this very Chain Pickerel was tagged and released into these waters over 200 years ago! That day, on 4th July 1796, many young fish were released with anchors tags bearing President’s George Washington’s signature to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence.

fish.name: Historic Chinook Salmon
fish.description: Chinook Salmon (Oncorhynchus Tshawytscha) are known to die after spawning. But it looks like this particular specimen chose a long and happy life over having offspring. Just imagine, this Chinook is over 200 years old! Judging by the anchor tag clipped onto its fin, this very fish had been tagged and released into these waters along with many other hatchlings on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Talk about capturing a piece of history!

fish.name: Historic Colorado Golden Trout
fish.description: Historic Colorado Golden Trout (Oncorhynchus Aguabonita) is a very unusual specimen of the Colorado Golden Trout. As a tiny hatchling, this fish was one of the special few that were tagged with the year 1796 and President’s George Washington’s signature and released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. How it lived up to this day - remains a mystery that might never be solved!

fish.name: Historic Cutthroat Trout
fish.description: Cutthroat Trout (Oncorhynchus Clarkii) is a well-known inhabitant of lakes and streams in the Rocky Mountains. Catching such a fish can sometimes lead to wondrous discoveries and this seems to be just the case! Just imagine, this very Cutthroat is one of the special hatchlings that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature!

fish.name: Historic Grass Pickerel
fish.description: This Grass Pike (Esox Americanus) is a truly historic specimen! There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year 1796 and bears President’s George Washington’s signature! Apparently, that very year special fish hatchlings were released on July 4th to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence.Talk about capturing a piece of history!

fish.name: Historic Largemouth Bass
fish.description: Largemouth Bass (Micropterus Salmoides) is the kind of fish you think you know everything about. But apparently this particular monster will prove to be quite a shock! Just imagine, this fish hatched into this world when horses were still the main means of transportation! In fact, this very Largemouth Bass was released into these waters along with many other young fish on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature!

fish.name: Historic Muskie
fish.description: Muskellunge (Esox Masquinongy) are like kings among predatory fish. Even huge monsters such as Catfish try to stay out of a Muskie’s way...no wonder these fish can live very long lives. But this particular Muskie is beyond old - judging by the anchor tag clipped onto its fin, it's one of the many young fish released into these waters over 200 years ago to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence! No doubt about it - the tag bears the release date and President George Washington's signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history! Long live the Muskie king!

fish.name: Historic Northern Pike
fish.description: Historic Northern Pike (Esox Lucius) is not just a fancy name! This fish is a real piece of history. The specimen bears a special anchor tag on its fin is marked with the year 1796 and bearing President’s George Washington’s signature! Apparently, that very year special fish hatchlings were released on July 4th to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Indeed, a truly historic specimen!

fish.name: Historic Rainbow Trout
fish.description: Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus Mykiss) are predatory fish with a very diverse diet. Neither mouse nor fish stand a chance if spotted by this hungry carnivore. Perhaps such a healthy appetite made it possible for this particular specimen to live over 200 years! No kidding, this very Rainbow Trout is one of the special hatchlings that were tagged with a special ring bearing President’s George Washington’s signature and released on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence.

fish.name: Historic Smallmouth Bass
fish.description: Smallmouth Bass (Micropterus Dolomieu) is perhaps one of the most popular game fish among anglers in North America. You’ve probably caught hundreds of these fish. But this time you’re in for a real surprise! When still just a hatchling, this very Smallmouth was released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature!

fish.name: Historic Spotted Bass
fish.description: This Spotted Bass (Micropterus Punctulatus) is older than history itself! This very fish is one of the special hatchlings that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history! Such cases of long-lifers among all species of Black Bass may be rare but not unknown to scientists, who have been trying in vain to solve this mystery for many years...

fish.name: Historic Steelhead Trout
fish.description: Historic Steelhead Trout (Oncorhynchus Mykiss) is an extremely unusual specimen of a Steelhead Trout. While all Steelheads are known to be aggressive predators that can live very long lives, this particular fish is beyond old - judging by the anchor tag clipped onto its fin, it's one of the many hatchlings released into these waters over 200 years ago to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence! No doubt about it - the tag bears the release date and President George Washington's signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history!

fish.name: Historic Striped Bass
fish.description: Striped Bass (Morone saxatilis) is generally a very resilient and die-hard fish. Known to tolerate both salt and fresh water, the oldest Striper ever recorded was 31 years of age. But looks like the specimen you just caught is way beyond anything in the book of World Records - this particular fish is over 200 years old! As unbelievable as it may be - there can be no doubt if you examine the anchor tag with President George Washington’s signature. It means that this Striper was one of the many young fish released into these waters on 4th July 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. Talk about luck!

fish.name: Historic Walleye
fish.description: Historic Walleye (Sander Vitreus) - this extremely rare specimen of Walleye is almost older than history itself! One of the special hatchlings that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence, the fish boasts an old anchor tag on its fin, marked with the year 1796 and President’s George Washington’s signature! Such cases of long-lifers among these historic fish are rare, but not entirely unknown to scientists, who have been trying in vain to solve this mystery for many years...

fish.name: Historic White Bass
fish.description: Historic White Bass (Morone Chrysops) belonging to the White Bass species, that are known to scientists are fish with rather stunning longevity, this particular specimen is older than history itself! Tagged and released into these very waters over 200 years ago, this fish was one of the hatchlings that were set free on July 4th 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence! There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin bears the engraved year and President George Washington’s initials!

fish.name: Historic White Crappie
fish.description: White Crappie (Pomoxis Annularis) are widespread panfish in North America with a relatively short lifespan. But you managed to catch an extremely rare specimen! This very White Crappie comes from the pool of young fish that were released into these waters on July 4th, 1796 to honor the 20th Anniversary of American Independence. There can be no doubt about it - the anchor tag clipped onto its fin is marked with the year and President’s George Washington’s signature! Talk about capturing a piece of history! The only question that remains a mystery is how this White Crappie manage to live such a long life...?

fish.name: Blue Bandit Aracu
fish.description: Okay, so you arrive at your fishing spot and see a bearded bandit looking at you from the water depth. What would you do? Why, catch the rascal and make him lead you to his boss – Crumbling Krampus Payara! This is how you can return the beard back to Santa and save Christmas. By the way, rumor has it that the Bandit Aracu is extremely fond of donuts.

fish.name: Blue Dunce Crappie
fish.description: Some think that glasses make you look smarter. But it doesn’t work if you are a dunce, such as this Crappie! He helped the Unlucky Krampus Tarpon to steal Santa’s glasses. And he is not sorry for doing it. Teach him a good lesson, and also find out where his boss is hiding. To catch more Crappies, make sure to stock up on cookies and milk. It’s their favorite snack!

fish.name: Blue Foolish Goby
fish.description: What would you call a Goby, who helped to steal a precious item of headwear from Santa? Now the Clumsy Krampus Eel has the hat, and it won’t be easy to find the villain without his Goby accomplice. But if you have some cookies, your chances to catch the troublemaker increase. So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

fish.name: Clumsy Krampus Eel
fish.description: What was this Clumsy Krampus Eel thinking, stealing Santa’s hat? Did he honestly want to deliver presents in a reindeer sleigh? Most likely he just had one too many drinks with his old mischievous Krampus pals, enjoying the party punch a bit too enthusiastically. But this character is not as simple as he looks. It will take some effort to get the hat back! However, we know for sure that the elderly Eel has a very sweet tooth and can’t resist a Christmas treat, such as cakes or stollen.

fish.name: Crumbling Krampus Payara
fish.description: Just look at this Crumbling Krampus Payara – she would gladly use her set of false teeth to snatch away anything that doesn’t belong to her. Who can tell why she would need Santa’s Beard? It’s plainly obvious that this fish is just an obnoxious old relic, tipsy on eggnog! No choice but to get some candy to catch the thief and make her give the Beard back, because Santa surely needs it!

fish.name: Decorated Alligator Gar
fish.description: Alligator Gars (Atractosteus spatula) are among the largest freshwater fish in North America. They are found in the southern regions of the United States extending down to Mexico and inhabit primarily large, slow-moving rivers, freshwater lakes, swamps, estuaries, and bays. These fish can breathe both air and water and bear a resemblance to American alligators, having torpedo-shaped bodies armored with nearly impenetrable scales and broad snouts with long sharp teeth. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Asp
fish.description: Asp (Leuciscus Aspius) is a European freshwater fish of the Carp family. It inhabits many of the large rivers that fall into the Black, Caspian and Baltic seas, as well as some waterways in the Middle East. Asp prefer waterways with moderate and fast paced current, usually staying closer to the surface. Asp can distinguished by its blue-gray body with silvery sides and white belly. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Chain Pickerel
fish.description: Chain Pickerel (Esox niger) is a species of freshwater fish in the pike family (Esocidae). Chain pickerel are usually yellowish-brown, with a distinctive pattern of interlocking dark bands on the sides that resembles a chain-link fence. The species prefers to stay in cover and is most often found in patches of aquatic vegetation, as they usually strike when unsuspecting prey swim their way. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Channel Catfish
fish.description: Channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus) is North America's most numerous catfish species and the most fished catfish species in the USA. They are most abundant in large streams with low or moderate current.And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Chum Salmon
fish.description: Chum Salmon (Oncorhynchus Keta) is a Pacific Salmon with the largest natural range of distribution and can be found among other places around the north Pacific, the Bering Sea, from Alaska to California in the United States, around British Columbia in Canada as well as in the waters of Korea and Japan. Chum are anadromous fish, meaning they migrate from the sea up into freshwater to spawn. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Colorado Golden Trout
fish.description: Colorado Golden Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss aguabonita), is a subspecies of the Rainbow Trout native to the state of Colorado. These fish are endemic to cold mountain lakes, rivers and streams in the Rocky Mountain region of Colorado. The Colorado Golden Trout is distinguished by spectacularly bright coloration of golden and vivid red, with horizontal bands on the sides. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Cutthroat Trout
fish.description: Cutthroat Trout (Oncorhynchus clarkii) is a fish species of the salmon family native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean, Rocky Mountains, and Great Basin in North America. This black-spotted game fish is named for its bright-red streaks beneath the lower jaws. Cutthroats usually inhabit shallow rivers with clear water and gravel bottoms as well as clear, cold, moderately deep lakes. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Ghost Carp
fish.description: Ghost Carp (Cyprinus Carpio Albino) is another artificially bred variation of the Common Carp, which is a hybrid of the Japanese fish Purachina Koi. Similar to Common Carp, the Ghost Carp prefers to inhabit large bodies of slow or standing water and soft, vegetative sediments. Commonly spread throughout Great Britain, these beautiful fish are easily distinguished by their coloration, which may vary ranging from bright white to yellowish-grey. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Lake Trout
fish.description: Lake Trout (Salvelinus Namaycush) is a freshwater fish and the largest of chars native to the lakes in the northern parts of North America, particularly the Great Lakes and Alaska. This species prefers to stay in cold, well oxygenated water and is prized by anglers both as a game fish and as a food fish. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Longnose Gar
fish.description: Longnose Gar (Lepisosteus osseus) is a primitive species of Gar present in North America for about 100 million years. These fish can be found in freshwater lakes along the east coast of North and Central America and as far west as Kansas and Texas. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Marble Trout
fish.description: Marble Trout (Salmo Marmoratus) is a European species of freshwater fish of the Salmon family. These fish can be found only in the northern parts of the Adriatic basin, some rivers in Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, and Montenegro. Marble Trout prefers to inhabit cold river and lakes close to mountainous areas. The Marble Trout has a large head and a long, cylindrical body, slightly compressed on the sides. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Prussian Carp
fish.description: Prussian Carp (Carassius Gibelio), also known as Silver Prussian Carp, is a freshwater game fish that originally came from Siberia and has been introduced throughout Europe, North America and Asia. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what ...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Red Drum
fish.description: Red Drum (Sciaenops ocellatus) is a game fish with a habitat from Massachusetts to Key West, Florida, and along the Gulf Coast to Mexico. Sometimes called Redfish or simply Red, these fish mostly prefer shallow areas of bays and estuaries with submerged vegetation and soft mud bottom. Red Drum are usually distinguished by a dark red color on the back, white belly and with one large black spot on the upper part of the tail. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Silver Carp
fish.description: Silver Carp (Hypophthalmichthys Molitrix) is a large freshwater fish of the Carp family native to East Asian rivers. These schooling fish primarily inhabit large rivers. Silver Carp have elongated bodies with gray-greenish backs, silvery sides, and underbelly. They are easily distinguished from other fish of the Carp family by their unusually low position of the eyes and large size. And what’s that? It looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Tiger Muskie
fish.description: Tiger Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy × lucius), commonly called Tiger Muskie, is a hybrid of the Muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) and the Northern Pike (Esox lucius). This carnivorous fish lives in freshwater lakes and rivers ranging from Canada, the Northeast, and to the Midwest United States. These fish grow stronger and faster than their parent fish and are quite a challenge to catch, therefore even called “Fish of 10,000 casts”. Tiger Muskies have vertical stripes on a light background, which is the opposite color scheme of a Northern Pike. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated White Crappie
fish.description: White Crappie (Pomoxis annularis) is a freshwater fish native to North America, that was successfully introduced to many other countries. This species is typically found in warm murky (turbid) rivers and lakes. Its body is silvery in color with dark lateral bars along its side and a white belly. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what ...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated White Sturgeon
fish.description: White Sturgeon (Acipenser Transmontanus), is a species of Sturgeon that is the largest freshwater fish in North America. These fish live on the bottoms of slow-moving rivers, bays, and estuarine areas along the west coast of North America from the Aleutian Islands to Central California. White Sturgeon have slender bodies, usually ranging in colour from greenish gray to light gray. These fish have no scales and are covered in armor of large bony plates. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Decorated Zander
fish.description: Zander (Sander Lucioperca) is a popular European game species of fish that is closely related to Perch and is often called the European Pikeperch. Although widespread in both freshwater and brackish habitats throughout western Eurasia, Zander prefer to inhabit large freshwater rivers and lakes. Sometimes called Pike-perch, Zander is even considered to be a hybrid of the two species, as it looks a lot like Pike due to its elongated body, while having a spiny dorsal fin, just like Perch. And what’s that? Looks like this fish has something stuck to its scales. And do you know what...it’s one of Santa’s lost Christmas Ornaments! Just what we need for decorating the holiday tree!

fish.name: Green Bandit Aracu
fish.description: Okay, so you arrive at your fishing spot and see a bearded bandit looking at you from the water depth. What would you do? Why, catch the rascal and make him lead you to his boss – Crumbling Krampus Payara! This is how you can return the beard back to Santa and save Christmas. By the way, rumor has it that the Bandit Aracu is extremely fond of donuts.

fish.name: Green Dunce Crappie
fish.description: Some think that glasses make you look smarter. But it doesn’t work if you are a dunce, such as this Crappie! He helped the Unlucky Krampus Tarpon to steal Santa’s glasses. And he is not sorry for doing it. Teach him a good lesson, and also find out where his boss is hiding. To catch more Crappies, make sure to stock up on cookies and milk. It’s their favorite snack!

fish.name: Green Foolish Goby
fish.description: What would you call a Goby, who helped to steal a precious item of headwear from Santa? Now the Clumsy Krampus Eel has the hat, and it won’t be easy to find the villain without his Goby accomplice. But if you have some cookies, your chances to catch the troublemaker increase. So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

fish.name: Red Bandit Aracu
fish.description: Okay, so you arrive at your fishing spot and see a bearded bandit looking at you from the water depth. What would you do? Why, catch the rascal and make him lead you to his boss – Crumbling Krampus Payara! This is how you can return the beard back to Santa and save Christmas. By the way, rumor has it that the Bandit Aracu is extremely fond of donuts.

fish.name: Red Dunce Crappie
fish.description: Some think that glasses make you look smarter. But it doesn’t work if you are a dunce, such as this Crappie! He helped the Unlucky Krampus Tarpon to steal Santa’s glasses. And he is not sorry for doing it. Teach him a good lesson, and also find out where his boss is hiding. To catch more Crappies, make sure to stock up on cookies and milk. It’s their favorite snack!

fish.name: Red Foolish Goby
fish.description: What would you call a Goby, who helped to steal a precious item of headwear from Santa? Now the Clumsy Krampus Eel has the hat, and it won’t be easy to find the villain without his Goby accomplice. But if you have some cookies, your chances to catch the troublemaker increase. So here’s the plan: catch the Goby, and use him to close in on his boss to return the stolen object!

fish.name: Unlucky Krampus Tarpon
fish.description: This old Tarpon has clearly had a bit too much eggnog. He’s not quite as menacing as in the days of old, but there is still fight left in him! At the very least, he was capable enough to nick Santa’ glasses. Alas, he forgot to give them back, which is not surprising, given his age. It would be a good idea to find the old guy and gently remind him that Santa needs his glasses more. The problem is, the Unlucky Tarpon has long since lost his lower jaw. Well, you’ll just have to use this special lure...

fish.name: Albino Blackfish
fish.description: Albino Blackfish (Dallia Albineus) infected by radiation from a toxic waste leak, these specimen of otherwise black Alaska Blackfish are absolutely white in color and seem to have a particularly insatiable craving for Salmon eggs. Although these infected fish are hardly over 0.3 kg (0.6 lb) in weight, they are rather numerous and therefore present a serious problem causing much damage to the populations of Salmon species.

fish.name: Black Whisker
fish.description: Black Whisker (Silurus Nigreos) - this huge whiskered monster has devoured so much fish in Sander Baggersee Lake, that its belly and eyes look like they are about to burst! Even so, the Black Whisker doesn't plan to stop its feeding frenzy, thus putting the lake’s entire ecosystem at risk. Not unless some fearless angler puts an end to this dark foodsie’s nightmare!

fish.name: Carp Colossus
fish.description: Colossus Carp (Cyprinidae Colossus) - a Carp unlike any you’ve ever seen, this colossal monstrous creature is terrorizing the peaceful waters of Weeping Willow fisheries! Even the largest trophy-sized species are terrified of this fat-bellied underwater titan, lurking in the murky depths. Will anyone find a way to lure the Colossus Carp out of its underwater lair?

fish.name: Cyber Piranha
fish.description: Piranhas are cautious and even shy, but Cyber Piranhas are completely devoid of natural behavior. These monsters are modified with various implants that make them incredibly dangerous. A mechanically strengthened body, cybernetic vision, sharp adamant-covered teeth, and the instincts of real schooling predators — this is exactly what terminator fish look like! But for every terminator, there is a melting furnace — or, in this case, an Electrical Leader.

fish.name: Dendrofin
fish.description: Dendrofin (Amia Dendronimus) this extremely fishy mutation of what used to be your ordinary Bowfin is the result of an ambush predator going vegan! After all, you are what you eat! Or so they say. At least, the Dendrofin would agree. Looks like this particular specimen swapped his ordinary carnivorous diet for genuine tree bark and now miraculously resembles an old log! Gotta hand it to the vegan diet - this powerful monster has grown to nearly 6 kg (13 lb) and is getting stronger by the day! Who cares how you look when you’re that big, right? But while sporting such a tree-like texture might be Dendrofin’s great camouflage, we sure know what kind of bait this wood-hungry monster won’t resist!

fish.name: Eel Cannibal
fish.description: Cannibal Eel (Anguilla Canibalium) was smuggled into the peaceful waters of Ghent-Terneuzen canal from Africa by rebellious trouble-makers. It looks horrifying enough to scare any angler out of their wits. This monster seems to have a particular taste for its own kind, heartlessly hunting for other Eels and decimating their population!

fish.name: Eldergar
fish.description: Eldergar (Lepisosteus Antiquus) is probably the oldest known Longnose Gar ever recorded. Having well outlived the typical lifespan of its own species, the Eldergar at least 70 years old, which is twice the age of the oldest specimen previously recorded! No wonder this old-timer is also the largest Longnose in history - weighing almost 25 kg (55 lb)! Ichthyologists believe the reason behind this anomaly to be found in the Eldergar’s feeding habits. It appears that this old-timer has taken to a very strange diet: not only does the Eldergar hunt exclusively on American Shad, but seems to be feeding entirely of their heads, leaving the rest of the Shad bodies to be eaten by scavengers.

fish.name: Elusive Arapaima
fish.description: This is probably the oldest and most cunning Arapaima you can ever encounter. The local legends say that this monster is the evil spirit of Lake Maku-Maku, who has lived there since time immemorial. Anyone who tried to catch it failed at best, and at worst — disappeared altogether! They say neither tridents, nor nets, nor strong tackle can take it on. However, there is a way for a brave angler to land this ancient fish!

fish.name: Fenrivore
fish.description: Legends say the Fenrivore was born from the cursed blood of Fenrir, the giant wolf fated to devour Odin at Ragnarök. When his blood spilled into the ocean during a fierce battle, the sea twisted the curse into flesh, shaping creatures with wide maws and wolf-sharp teeth. Drawn together by that same dark hunger, the Fenrivores hunt in packs, striking swiftly to claim as many victims as the deep will offer. To this day, local anglers whisper that these horrors are the ocean’s omen of Ragnarök.

fish.name: Fighter Shark
fish.description: Young sharks are known to often become prey to local caimans. However, this particular monster has won many battles with the sharp-toothed reptiles. Its hundreds of scars and the only remaining eye speak eloquently about its victories. Having gained strength and experience, the monster itself became a menace to the caimans, which are worshiped by the local tribe!

fish.name: Ghost Peacock Bass
fish.description: Ghost Peacock Bass (Cichla Exspiravit) - this pale, red-eyed monster seems to stir quite a panic among all other fish, making it impossible for anglers to enjoy their favorite pastime at this waterway! Seen only at night, the Ghost Peacock Bass will turn anyone who catches it into a real ghostbusting hero in the eyes of the local angling community!

fish.name: Gourmet Bass
fish.description: Gourmet Bass (Morone Gurmanius) this huge specimen is way over the size of any freshwater Bass you could hope to catch! Weighing roughly 30 kg (75 lb), the Gourmet Bass gets its size and name from its highly gourmet dietary habits. Apparently, it developed quite a taste for nutritious, protein-rich foods and will eat any molluscs it can find!

fish.name: Grayling Wrestler
fish.description: Grayling Wrestler (Thymallus Luctator) is a monstrous type of European Grayling with a temper so malicious that it has turned its color to dark, almost black! It’ll take some wits and skills to catch this mad fighter!

fish.name: Grouperzilla
fish.description: Grouperzilla is a creature born from the depths of the polluted oceans, where an ordinary huge grouper transformed into a giant sea monster. It’s known for its considerable size and strength, far exceeding any known representative of its species. Grouperzilla is known for its aggressive behavior and insatiable appetite. It often hunts for its favorite snack — lobsters — and can attack the boats of anglers who have this delicacy on board.

fish.name: Helgaflut
fish.description: Once upon a time, Odin punished the people for their greed, sending a harsh winter that emptied the sea and brought hunger to the villages. However, his wife Frigg, moved by pity for the families and their children, wept into the empty waters, turning her tears into Helgaflut. With a sacred fire in their hearts, these fish melted the ice and saved the people of Isvikheimen from hungry death. From that day on, every angler who catches Helgafllut is granted a year of good fortune and full keepnets.

fish.name: Hordecuda
fish.description: The sunlit atolls of the Maldives have been thrown into chaos by a terrifying phenomenon — the Horde of Barracudas. Typically, adult Barracudas are solitary hunters, but now they have united into a relentless, predatory gang. This wild horde tears through the reefs, leaving nothing but destruction and panic in its wake. Moving with uncanny coordination, they hunt as one, instantly surrounding their prey and giving it no chance to escape. A Horde of Barracudas isn't just a danger — it's a force of nature. In the Maldives, they are known as the Hordecuda.

fish.name: Mad-Eye Buffalo
fish.description: Mad-Eye Buffalo (Ictiobus Oculus) Considered to be a figment of some anglers’ imagination, the Mad-Eye Buffalo is nevertheless very real and is in fact a rare and extremely strange mutation of the freshwater Smallmouth Buffalo. This monstrous fish gets its name for having magically sharp eyesight that, legend has it, allows it to see through anything - from walls to the human soul. It can also spot the most intricate details in any light, which means, that catching this monster will require using some of the thinnest and frailest fishing like you can find! Quite a challenge, considering that the Mad-Eye weighs around 6 kg (13 lb)!

fish.name: Mega Piranha
fish.description: Nobody knows whose evil genius combined the most voracious fish in South America with the latest achievements in biomechatronics to create incredibly powerful cyborg monsters! Razor-sharp teeth made from solid adamant, improved bodies with mechanical fins, cyber vision, and inherent bloodthirstiness — what else do ideal killer fish need? To tackle one of these monstrosities, you’ll need a miracle — or an Adamant Leader!

fish.name: Mighty M'Benga
fish.description: Local legends say that the Congo is home to an evil spirit named M'Benga, which can possess river dwellers. It seems that this spirit has inhabited a particularly large specimen of Goliath Tigerfish. The spirit grants the monster fish demonic strength and bloodthirstiness. According to the legend, only the blood of its fellow species and a special ritual performed by a real shaman can temporarily calm the fury of M'Benga. So hurry up — you don't have much time!

fish.name: Muskie Golem
fish.description: Muskie Golem (Esox Stonius) - there are many fish legends among the anglers of Saint Croix Lake, one of which is about the Muskie Golem. This fish gets its name for having abnormally large and tough scales that make it look as if made of rock. The Muskie Golem is also said to be well over a hundred years old and weighs almost 35 kg (75 lb), which makes it the largest Muskie specimen in all of Saint Croix! Virtually uncatchable, as it seems to take no interest in any typical baits or lures.

fish.name: Night Windrazor
fish.description: In the tropical waters of the Maldives, where moonlight glides over the waves, sailors whisper of the Night Razor — a legendary Sailfish Monster. This sleek predator moves between lagoons in a heartbeat, leaving behind only a sharp, silvery flash. Some mistake it for moonlight, but seasoned fishermen know the truth — when you see that flash, the Night Razor is hunting. Unlike ordinary Sailfish, this one hides in the deep to stalk Luminous Flying Fish that stand out even at night. Night Razor's ruthless hunting style and raw strength make it a formidable challenge to catch.

fish.name: Perch Bully
fish.description: Perch Bully (Perca Corruptor) is a ferocious predator unlike any Perch you’ve ever seen! Relentlessly hunting down its prey and devouring any fish it can bite into with its big mouth and razor sharp teeth, the Perch Bully can only be caught using a special type of lure!

fish.name: Pikeslasher
fish.description: Pikeslasher (Sander Murderus) a genuine mystery to ichthyologists, the Pikeslasher is a blood-thirsty mutation of the common Walleye that has developed quite a taste for Pike! Who knows, perhaps this is a fishy case of personal vendetta, a thrilling story of Walleye vengeance for a loved one that was heartlessly, yet naturally, consumed by Pike sometime in the past... We’ll probably never know the Pikeslasher’s true motives. But what we do know, is that this gigantic carnivorous monster has adopted the coloration of a Pike and now weighs about 10 kg (22 lb)! Looks like you’ll need to make some first rate pike cutbait to trick the Pikeslasher into biting.

fish.name: Rainbow Outlaw
fish.description: Rainbow Outlaw (Oncorhynchus Genetikus) this abnormally large specimen of a lake form Rainbow Trout was apparently sneaky enough to escape from one of Oregon’s trout farms, where it was genetically engineered to grow extra-large. The oversized runaway resorted to some meticulous route planning to make its escape - using a network of underground streams it traveled between different lakes until settling down in Falcon’s peaceful waters. But while this genetically modified organism succeeded in covering its tracks from the fish farmers, it’s huge size of over 25 kg (50 lb) is a dead giveaway. And feeding exclusively on Brown Trout Eggs, the Rainbow Outlaw is only getting bigger.

fish.name: Striped Blade
fish.description: The Striped Blade Monster is an incredible Marlin known for its speed and aggressiveness. Its long, sword-like snout is supernaturally tough, allowing it to cut through even the strongest fishing nets. The iridescent stripes on this Monster’s body serve as a warning sign in the underwater environment, clearly indicating who’s in charge here. These stripes also emit a faint glow, which creates the impression of dancing light in the dark depths of the ocean and attracts underwater creatures. This graceful and powerful monster will become the jewel of any sophisticated collection.

fish.name: Sturgeon Leviathan
fish.description:
Leviathan Sturgeon (Acipenseridae Pristis) is a huge monster fish found in the Dnipro River. Known for its impressive size and strength, this fish is a dream catch for adventurous anglers looking for a thrilling challenge. To reel in this unique giant, you'll need a combination of skill, a bit of luck, and some special lures.

Cookies and Mussels Groundbait

fish.name: Taimen-Khan
fish.description: This huge Taimen has no competitors because of its impressive size. This is an excellent hunter who is constantly on the move. This Taimen is not too picky in terms of food: it’s happy to eat rodents and waterfowl that have fallen into the water as well as small fish. According to old-timers, it once used to drag dogs into the deep. This specimen is rightfully considered the Khan of the entire Selenge River.

fish.name: Terror Tarpon
fish.description: Terror Tarpon (Megalops Terroristus) looking scarred and hostile, this highly aggressive Tarpon came to the quiet marshy areas of the Everglades from the brackish coastal prairies and is terrorizing the local fish. Although relatively average in size, weighing just about 20 kg (44 lb), this feisty trouble maker is doing a lot of damage to the underwater ecosystem of this area by seriously diminishing the population of Largemouth Bass, which it seems to have a particular taste for.

fish.name: Thorn-Ripper
fish.description: The Thorn-Ripper is an aggressive monster fish that lives in the depths of the Dnipro River. Its spikes grew over centuries of survival among predators, serving as both defense and weapon. Legends say that humans once fished out its family, and since then, the Thorn-Ripper has been seeking revenge on fishermen by piercing boats with its spikes. When it hears the sound of a boat above its territory, it swiftly attacks, puncturing it like needles. Fishermen now fear encountering this underwater menace. Since this fish is extremely cautious, only a unique lure like the Wasp Walker can capture its interest.

fish.name: Tyrannotrout
fish.description: Tyrannotrout (Oncorhynchus Tyrannosaurus) a.k.a the T-Rex Trout, is a carnivorous prehistoric monster of the Salmon family that has inexplicably infested the waters of one of New York’s most calm and peaceful lakes! Being a fairly small fish of under 1 kg (2.2 lb), a single T-Rex Trout couldn’t do much harm. Except from, maybe, biting your hand off. However, these razor-toothed flesh-hungry monsters hunt in schools and are endangering the entire population of fish in Rocky Lake! As there’s plenty of easy prey for these beasts to devour, the only way to get a Tyrannotrout’s attention is by using a special turtle-shell prehistoric lure.

fish.name: Voodoo Fish
fish.description: Voodoo Fish (Lota Magicus) according to an old indian legend, this mythical fish belongs to an extinct species that possessed magical powers and was a distant ancestor of today’s Burbot. Apparently the last remaining specimen of its kind, this age-old monster dwells in an abysmal hole somewhere in the deepest part of White Moose Lake and comes out to roam closer to the lake’s surface every once in a blue moon! No one knows exactly how long this archaic creature has lived for, but judging from the ancient markings of Northern indigenous tribes on its back, the Voodoo Fish was a part of some magical rituals that date back to over a century!

fish.name: Wailing Catfish
fish.description: This huge and greedy catfish was nicknamed Wailing for a reason. The low sounds emitted by this giant resemble underwater growling and can be heard hundreds of yards away from the Marron River. Its cries spreading through the jungle can scare not only fish and animals, but also people. And although it’s known for certain that some catfish can make loud sounds, no ichthyologists have ever heard such a roar. Rest assured, they would give a lot to get their hands on such a specimen!

fish.name: Zombie Cat
fish.description: Zombie Cat (Mortuus Consumus) while all Catfish are bottom-feeding scavengers in general, and among other things may consume dead fish, this particular whiskery monster has taken such an uncomely diet to the extreme. Gravely and old, the Zombie Cat feeds exclusively on any rotten and decaying organisms it can find on the bottom of swampy Quanchkin Lake. Looking rather like a monster from a Pet Cemetery horror sequel, this consumer of death is spreading a putrid smell all around the area!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Heavy Chaser
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ presents Heavy Chaser™ - the new, most powerful bottom fishing rod designed with enough backbone and endurance to handle the biggest and heaviest fish imaginable! Be it fierce sturgeon or heavyweight trophy cats, this rod is built with all of the top technologies at its core to provide brilliant performance and unmatched strength when battling any record-sized underwater adversary!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Cat Boxer
gear.description: Cat Boxer™ is a conventional and versatile fishing rod from UL-CHUBER™, created especially for bottom fishing and designed for handling large and heavy fish, like trophy cats! Built to last, the Cat Boxer™ features at its core all of the company’s technological advancements and is the perfect choice particularly when fishing from a boat.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Bottom Sniper
gear.description: Proudly opening the line of top quality bottom rods from UL-CHUBER™, the BottomSniper™ is a versatile fishing weapon with amazing casting potential. Although with a lower line weight rating, the BottomSniper™ is indeed one of the most long-range bottom rods that will provide flawless performance throughout any bottom fishing escapades. Cured based on the HyperTension™ high frequency method, and built using state-of-the-art ProtoFibre™ material, the BottomSniper™ has an extremely resilient blank that is simply unmatched when making those powerful, long-distance casts. Choose your version of this delightfully powerful rod from 3 different lengths.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ La Cazadora™
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ has designed this powerful bottom rod specifically for South American fishing. A magnificent combination of durability, power and ease allows you to be confident in your fights with some serious underwater inhabitants! Don’t be surprised by its small size. Thanks to new technologies, this rod can hold real bottom-dwelling monsters, including the giant catfish species like Piraiba or Gilded Catfish.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Mokonzi™
gear.description: The Mokonzi™ rod is a perfect combination of power, range potential, and usability. As with many of their products, the UL-Chuber™ experts used ProtoFibre® technology in the rod blanks to reinforce the carbon fibers, making the rod both powerful and lightweight. Plus, its ergonomic handle is comfortable to hold thanks to the unique TrueGrip® coating, which significantly enhances both the rod performance and the overall fishing experience. It’s no longer a problem to land any giant bottom dweller: you can rely on the experience and advanced technologies used when making this rod.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Heavy Chaser Sport
gear.description: Presenting the much awaited sports series of fishing rods with a chic and stylish black-n-white design that puts emphasis on the word SPORT in sportfishing! This sportfishing rod is twice as strong and durable as its original predecessor. UL-CHUBER™ presents Heavy Chaser™ Sport - the new, most powerful bottom fishing rod designed with enough backbone and endurance to handle the biggest and heaviest fish imaginable! Be it fierce sturgeon or heavyweight trophy cats, this rod is built with all of the top technologies at its core to provide brilliant performance and unmatched strength when battling any record-sized underwater adversary!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Heavy Chaser Golden Edition
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ Heavy Chaser Golden Edition

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ X-Series Frogman™
gear.description: Finally a thing worthy of winners! Created from advanced composite materials, it has an incredible combination of strength and ergonomics. The creators focused on its resistance to added loads and created a truly effective tool that will allow you to catch the strongest bottom monsters of record size with maximum comfort and pleasure.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ WCC Heavy Chaser™
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ is proud to present this unique bottom rod designed specifically for the World Cats Cup. This light but strong rod will allow you to take on even the largest underwater dwellers. Unsurpassed quality, latest technologies, and innovative materials will give you an unforgettable experience of professional bottom fishing. And the memorable tournament-themed design is sure to set you apart from other anglers. This rod will definitely increase your chances of winning the tournament!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ WCC La Cazadora™
gear.description: Just for the World Cats Cup, UL-CHUBER™ has developed this powerful bottom rod to help you reach the heights of competitive bottom fishing! Thanks to the combination of lightness, durability, and amazing power, this rod can be your key to tackling even the largest fish. The design and colors in the style of the tournament will only emphasize your status of a professional angler. With this excellent tackle, the victory is practically in your pocket!

gear.name: Humerus
gear.description: This bottom rod with a humerus handle is ideal for resisting the invasion of otherworldly evil spirits that have overtaken the reservoirs. Light, strong, and incredibly powerful, it is ready to fight even the fiercest inhabitants of the bottom depths. Meet your opponents fully armed!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ X-Series Omega
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ once again offers a wonderful prize for all bottom fishing tournament winners! Everything is perfect in this rod: increased strength, unprecedented power, and ease of use! Despite its rather modest size, it is designed for catching really large bottom fish. Be sure that this tackle can conquer any giant Catfish!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ LBFC DeepDiver
gear.description: Rivertex™ has brought you a stylish, innovative LBFC DeepDiver 310 bottom rod custom designed for the Live Bait Fiesta Cup. Its superior performance makes it easy for the angler to land bottom dwellers. The rod is constructed using MaxCarbon® technology, which ensures that the carbon fibers are evenly spaced during the building of the blank, which contributes to a significant increase in strength. Its power can help it manage even the heftiest catch. With such a rod you are guaranteed to always come out on top in battles with bottom monsters!

gear.name: Tribal Totem
gear.description: Tribal Totem™, a unique bottom rod designed specially for the Halloween event, decorated with vibrant African patterns and infused with the power of ancient tribes. Tribal Totem™ is created to battle the wild and elusive Dingonek monster, known across cursed waters for its ferocity and strength. This rod combines durability and elegance, perfect for taming the most powerful underwater beasts. The influence of totem magic will help you conquer the creature and triumph in this chilling Halloween challenge!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Deep Horizon
gear.description: Deep Horizon™ is by far the most powerful top-line carp rod with the biggest casting potential from the UL-CHUBER™ brand. Featuring moderate-fast action, Deep Horizon™ was designed particularly for ideal long-distance casting! This top-notch carp rod has all of UL-CHUBER™ top technologies woven into its very core, including the state-of-the-art ProtoFibre™ material and the HyperTension™ high frequency curing method used for blank creation, making this carp rod able to withstand extreme pressure loads. Deep Horizon™ is equipped with the highest grade OxyTitan™ guides as well as the pleasantly sturdy TrueGrip™ handles, and can be rightfully called the most powerful of all existing carp rods created up to this moment!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Carp Ranger
gear.description: Carp Ranger™ is a new, top-notch bottom fishing rod from UL-CHUBER™ that takes carp fishing to a whole new level! Super powerful and resilient, the Carp Ranger™ has moderate-slow action and ensures unsurpassed casting potential as well as overall flawless performance due to the highest technological advancements at its core. Built using state-of-the-art ProtoFibre™ material and cured with the HyperTension™ high frequency method, this rod feature blanks that can withstand extreme pressure loads. Equipped with the highest grade OxyTitan™ guides, the Carp Ranger™ is one of the toughest high-quality carp rod on the market today!

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ Mega Chuber
gear.description: UL-CHUBER™ proudly presents Mega Chuber™ - a top-notch line of feeder rods that was engineered for powerful long casting and flawless performance throughout all bottom fishing techniques. Built using state-of-the-art ProtoFibre™ material and cured with the HyperTension™ high frequency method, these rods feature blanks that can withstand extreme pressure loads and are ideal for fishing with heavy and superheavy feeders. Superior power and shock resistance make Mega Chuber™ the toughest high-quality feeder rod on the market! Equipped with the highest grade OxyTitan™ guides, Mega Chuber™ are available in 3 lengths.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ MCT McCarp
gear.description: Presented to the angling world by UL-CHUBER™, this limited MCT tournament edition carp rod marks the occasion of this September’s exciting bottom fishing tournament that’s all about landing big fat Carp! This unique champion-potential rod is a mighty powerful fishing tool exclusively designed in the style and color theme of Mighty Carp Tour - all to make sure you’re armed with the best equipment for catching this tricky critter! Superb casting action and unrivaled performance capacity make the MCT McCarp™ carp rod an extremely versatile collectible with genuinely high performance fit for a confident Tournament winner.

gear.name: UL-CHUBER™ X-Series Katana™
gear.description: When it comes to the championship fight with Karp, the choice of weapons is crucial! Meet the most powerful carp-fishing tool today. Its base is lightweight but durable carbon fiber blank wich can withstand a strong tug, as well as a continuous heavy load. A perfect example of a combination of top technology, refined design and convenience.

gear.name: Tibia
gear.description: This carp rod with a tibia handle is the best way to get ready for the battle with otherworldly creatures! Light and at the same time very strong, it is ideal for catching evil Carps! And do not worry, its power will be enough to cope with any abomination from the other world.

gear.name: MagFin™ BassCaster
gear.description: BassCaster™ Part of our UltraCast® line rods, BassCaster™ is a true bass classic! An accurate, lightweight and balanced-action casting rod that is simply perfect for fishing in heavy corners and around tight covers. The DynoSpeed® blank construction complete with world’s most lightweight LGT® guides make this is an all-round high quality bass fishing rod that puts its focus on accuracy rather than distance.

gear.name: MagFin™ FarCaster
gear.description: The moment you take a FarCaster™ into your hands, it becomes clear that this is a true high-performance angling tool. This extremely accurate, well-balanced casting rod is easy to cast and perfect for deep-water applications. Featuring MagFin’s superior DynoSpeed® construction and EZGuide® technologies, the FarCaster™ is designed to handle big fish especially in open-water locations where heavy cover isn’t much of a problem.

gear.name: MagFin™ Jester
gear.description: This totally versatile and pleasantly affordable high quality series of StartCast® basic casting rods is a true delight for any beginner-level angler eager to tackle the intricate science of angling. The reliable and durable ProSpeed® blank along with the lightness of LGT® guides and line control of our hi-end EZGuide® system give you a high-performance casting rod you can count on for all-purpose fishing needs.

gear.name: Garry Scott™ Argo
gear.description: This professional casting rod series of the GSPro® rod line is designed for those who demand only the very best in rod technology. The Argo™ series incorporates exclusive Garry Scott™ UZZ® pattern technology to give you casting rods with truly amazing actions and dramatically higher sensitivity. This along with the MegaResin® hi-end blank technology really sets the Argo™ casting rods apart from the rest. Superbly balanced and exquisitely precise, all models within the series have balanced moderate to fast actions perfectly suited for playing any fish.

gear.description: Part of our Infinitor® prime line, the GalaxyCast® series presents the ultimate casting rod on the market. The blank is made from ultra slim high modulus MaxCarbon® alloy that is reinforced with ResinFix® unique curing technology for unified wall structure, reduced weight and improved performance. And while skills and techniques are the key attributes of any Champion, choosing the right fishing weapon is of paramount importance. In this aspect, you just can’t go wrong with the best!

gear.name: SwordCast™

gear.name: MagFin™ LuxCaster™

Indeed, let there be light!
